review.title: The application serves itself on loopback, hardened, as a standalone sidecar
review.acceptance: The desktop target builds a Next standalone server that a shell can spawn, and every control docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 7 names is implemented and tested. REQUIRED: output 'standalone' is set for the desktop target and only for it -- the document specifies it in two places and next.config.ts sets it in none, which is the single largest gap between the recorded design and the code. REQUIRED: the server binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly and never 0.0.0.0, asserted by a test rather than by configuration alone, because Next reads HOSTNAME from the environment and an inherited value would silently expose the listener to the LAN. REQUIRED: a per-launch 256-bit CSPRNG bearer token passed through the environment, required on every request, with a constant-time comparison and a refusal that does not state whether the token was absent or wrong. REQUIRED: Host header validation against the exact expected literal, because a bearer token does not stop DNS rebinding. REQUIRED: the application emits its own Content-Security-Policy, because Tauri's CSP injection stops applying the moment the frontend is a URL rather than bundled assets -- this is a real loss the document names and nothing currently replaces it. REQUIRED: the sidecar reports its actually-bound port on stdout rather than being told which port to use; a pick-then-bind handshake is a TOCTOU race and is refused. NOT IN SCOPE: the Rust shell, which is PW-0102.

Also run separately on the same tree: npm run lint -> 11/11, exit 0, ZERO warnings (two dead `Link` imports were left behind when the copied topbars were deleted and are removed rather than suppressed), and npm run build -> 11/11, exit 0, which is the first build of this repository with output:"standalone" set for the desktop target.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 7a8de45. npx vitest run src/lib/sidecar in apps/web -> 2 files, 23 tests, exit 0. Whole workspace: npx vitest run in apps/web -> 56 files, 964 tests, exit 0. EVERY TEST IS A REFUSAL WITH ITS ACCEPTANCE AS A PAIR, because a guard whose suite only shows it admitting a good request proves nothing. Specifically: an absent token is refused (any local process can reach a loopback port -- there is no OS boundary between a game launcher and this server); a valid token on a rebound Host is refused (DNS rebinding makes the VICTIM'S browser issue the request, so it already holds the token and only the Host check fires); a Host differing only in port is refused (that is another listener); an EMPTY token still ARMS the guard rather than disarming it, because readSidecarEnvironment uses Object.hasOwn and not truthiness, and an empty string is a deliberate value elsewhere in this repository; and all three refusals are asserted to be BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the wire cannot be used as an oracle telling an attacker which control it had already satisfied. START-TIME REFUSALS: a token under 256 bits, an unstated Host, and -- the one that matters most -- an UNSET HOSTNAME, because Next binds 0.0.0.0 when it is unset and a sidecar that inherited a container environment would serve the whole network with a token the user's own browser holds. Defaulting it would have hidden exactly that, so it is refused with the string 0.0.0.0 in the detail. The CSP is asserted to carry no wildcard, no inline script, object-src none and frame-ancestors none, and NOT to widen when given no origins. The handshake parser refuses a non-loopback host, because the shell points a webview at whatever it reports. The build-target guard still passes (26 tests), so output:"standalone" did not disturb the desktop module-resolution split. ONE HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND REPORTED: the first version of the no-runtime-switch test read the raw source and failed on this module's own COMMENT explaining why it does not read LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET -- the same shape of defect PL-0701's restatement guard hit. It now strips comments, which is what build-target.test.ts already does, and carries a non-vacuity assertion so the stripper cannot be eating the file.

review.title: An application shell: one layout, one navigation model, one token layer
review.acceptance: The application has a real shell, and the eight hand-copied topbars become one. MEASURED STARTING POINT: layout.tsx is sixteen lines -- html, body, children -- and the topbar is duplicated by hand in eight files, each with a slightly different status badge and a different or absent nav; the nav itself is four fragment anchors, and /search is reachable from no link anywhere in the application. REQUIRED: one persistent chrome in the root layout, with every route's copy deleted rather than left beside it. REQUIRED: a navigation model that reaches every screen that exists, including search; a dead link is worse than an absent one because it teaches a viewer the feature is broken. REQUIRED: a token layer -- spacing, type, radius, elevation, colour -- replacing eight dark-only variables and the px literals around them, and a light theme or an explicit recorded decision that this product is dark-only. REQUIRED: a skip link, a focus indicator defined globally rather than only inside two CSS modules, and Windows display scaling at 100/125/150/200 percent without clipping. NOT IN SCOPE: replacing any working server-side logic; this task is the shell the existing screens hang in.

review.title: Routes authorize the caller, and a launch token is not a login
review.acceptance: Sensitive application routes authorize WHO is calling them, and possession of the desktop launch token is never mistaken for that. THE R4 FINDING, QUOTED: docs/SECURITY.md records that 'no authentication or authorization exists on any API route yet' and that 'nothing in the current code should be read as a decision that these routes are safe to leave anonymous'. Acceptable for a web demo; not for a shipped desktop application with a loopback listener. THIS TASK IS DELIBERATELY NOT PW-0101 AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. PW-0101 owns the LISTENER boundary -- loopback-only bind, per-launch bearer, Host validation, CSP, the port handshake -- which answers 'may this process talk to the sidecar at all'. This task answers 'may this caller perform this operation', and the two are different questions with different failure modes. A single machine-wide token that satisfied both would mean every process on the user's PC, and every page the webview ever loads, holds full authority over every profile. REQUIRED, each proven mechanically rather than asserted: (1) a protected route requires an authenticated account/session context and refuses without one; (2) a profile-scoped route authorizes the ACTIVE OR OWNED profile and never trusts a profile id supplied by the caller -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable ProfileScope as a cross-profile data-access bypass and this is the route-level half of that same defect; (3) a playback or session operation does not become authorized merely because the caller holds the desktop launch token, asserted by a test that presents a valid token and no account context and requires a refusal; (4) a refusal does not leak resource existence where an existing contract requires that property, so 'not yours' and 'not there' are indistinguishable on the wire; (5) loopback origin is NEVER treated as authentication -- a test must present a request from 127.0.0.1 with no credential and require a refusal, because 'it came from this machine' is the exact assumption that makes a local listener a privilege-escalation surface. REQUIRED: the authorization decision is made in ONE place and the routes call it, rather than each handler deciding -- a second opinion about who may read a profile is how the first one stops being enforced. USES THE EXISTING SEAM: packages/auth and the ProfileScope minted by PL-0405 are adopted and wrapped, not replaced.
review.notes: R4 OWNERSHIP, DECIDED AND REPORTED BEFORE THE WORK STARTS, as gpt-architect's round-80 ruling item 7 requires. No existing PW task owns the route-authorization seam cleanly: PW-0101 owns the listener and the ruling explicitly forbids broadening it into application auth merely because it already carries a security-review gate; PW-0401 owns authentication of the desktop forwarder's counterparty, which is a different service and a different caller; PW-0303 is a profiles UI and owns no route. So this is the 'one narrowly scoped PW security task' the ruling permits. It sits in Track 4 rather than in a seventh track, because the six tracks are approved and this is the same seam as PW-0401 seen from the other side -- who may call, rather than what the callee proves. The surface is the three profile-scoped handlers plus one authorization module, and it deliberately does not include the route.ts files or the contracts: if enforcement turns out to need them, that is a surface widening to state at review, not to pre-reserve. DEPENDENCY EDGE ON PW-0101 REMOVED, ROUND 82, AND THE REMOVAL IS THE POINT. It was written as a hard dependency to express "the listener exists first", and that is a READ relationship, not a build one: this task writes apps/web/src/lib/authorization and three handlers, none of which PW-0101 touches, and its negative proof -- a valid launch token with no account context is REFUSED -- needs only that the token concept exist to be refused, which it now does and is committed. requireAllDependenciesDone would have held this BACKLOG until PW-0101 cleared review, which is the PL-0311 deadlock shape: a false edge gating work that does not actually depend on it. apps/web/src/lib/sidecar stays in reviewDependencies, which is where the real relationship belongs.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on b07c535. npm run typecheck at the root, own invocation, turbo 21/21, exit 0. Also npm run lint -> 11/11, zero problems.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on b07c535. npx vitest run src/lib/authorization -> 2 files, 27 tests, exit 0. Monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20, exit 0. THE FIVE PROOFS THE RULING REQUIRES, EACH AS A REFUSAL, because an authorization suite that mostly shows permitted callers being permitted proves the happy path and nothing about the boundary. (1) A protected route refuses with no account -- and a PROFILE route refuses on the account floor BEFORE the profile is examined, asserted by requiring the internal detail not to mention profile access, because evaluating the profile first would make "no such profile" observable to somebody who is not logged in. (2) The decision function takes NO profile id at all, asserted structurally against the source: there is no parameter a caller-supplied id could arrive through, which is the route-level form of the forgeable-ProfileScope bypass PL-0405 recorded. (3) THE LAUNCH TOKEN IS NOT A LOGIN, proven by the type signature rather than by a test that passes a header and checks it was ignored -- authorizeRoute is never given a Request, so it cannot consult the token even by accident, and the source is asserted to contain no bare `Request` type, no `headers`, and no `sidecar`. The behavioural half is there too: a caller that satisfied PW-0101's listener guard completely and carries no account is refused as unauthenticated. (4) All three not_permitted causes -- not owned, no ownership record, no active profile -- are BYTE-IDENTICAL on the wire, asserted as a one-element Set over wireDetail and over code, while STAYING DISTINCT in the internal detail, because hiding the difference from the operator too would make an authorization failure indistinguishable from a routing bug. 404 is refused for a profile the caller may not see, for the same reason. (5) LOOPBACK IS NEVER AUTHENTICATION: the source may not contain 127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost, x-forwarded-for or remoteAddress, with a non-vacuity assertion so the comment stripper is not eating the file. SECOND FILE, handler-authorization.test.ts, guards what the audit found ALREADY CORRECT across all three profile-scoped handlers: each resolves a request context; none reads a profile id by any of four spellings; the two data handlers authorize the ACTIVE profile via resolveActiveProfileScope; the external reason vocabulary cannot name a missing profile, asserted against the union declaration in packages/auth; and no handler mentions an address or the launch token. The profiles picker is exempt AND NAMED -- selection necessarily runs before any profile is active, which is why @liberty/auth publishes a separate selection decision. It opens with a non-vacuity check that every guarded file was actually read. TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND AND REPORTED RATHER THAN WIDENED AWAY: an assertion forbidding the word Request matched RequestAccountResolution and was narrowed by removing the known identifiers first, not by dropping the check; and an assertion bounding the external reason union by a 300-character window reached into the narrowing switch below it, where profile_not_found legitimately appears as a case -- that is the mapping working, not the leak -- and is now bounded to the declaration itself.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
